column2: On the authority of ʿAbdullāh ibn Busr, who said: “A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, the laws of Islam have become too many, so [tell us of] a comprehensive door to which we can hold fast. He said: Let your tongue remain moist with the remembrance of Allah.”
Recorded by Imam Aḥmad in abridged form with this wording.
Sharāʾiʿ al-Islām (“the laws of Islam”): its branches and qualities.
“A door to which we can hold fast”: direct us to a door that we can keep to in practice,
jāmiʿ (“comprehensive”): all-embracing, easy to act on and perform, and of great reward.
Raṭban (“moist”): fresh, constantly uttering the remembrance of Allah.
(Note) The questioner wanted a deed besides the obligations; he did not mean to make it suffice in place of the obligations and duties, but wanted to do more alongside performing the obligations.
The virtue of persevering in the remembrance of Allah the Exalted.
Considering people's circumstances: perhaps the Messenger ﷺ saw that this man was unable to carry out deeds other than remembrance.
Remembrance is the best of words for whoever perseveres in it, and it gathers good and happiness.

In this hadith a man from among the noble Companions asked the Messenger ﷺ to direct him to something easy, comprehensive and inclusive of the qualities of goodness, and the Messenger ﷺ guided him to the remembrance of Allah, saying: “Let your tongue remain moist,

that is, fresh, with the remembrance of Allah”, repeating it constantly through the hours of night and day. He ﷺ chose it for him because it is light and easy for him, its reward is multiplied and its benefits are great beyond counting; their source is the Mighty Qurʾān and the many hadiths that have come on its virtue and benefits,

among them the saying of the Exalted: “O you who believe, remember Allah with much remembrance, and glorify Him morning and evening” [al-Aḥzāb 33:41–42]; “and remember Allah much, that you may succeed” [al-Jumuʿah 62:10]; “Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured” [al-Raʿd 13:28].

The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever would like to graze in the gardens of Paradise, let him remember Allah much”; and he (blessings and peace be upon him) said: “Two phrases are light on the tongue, beloved to the Most Merciful,
heavy in the Balance: Subḥān Allāh wa-bi-ḥamdih, Subḥān Allāh al-ʿAẓīm.” Among what has been said about remembrance:
Hours of remembrance are wealth and riches, / and hours of idle play are bankruptcy and want.
Remember Him much on earth, always, / so that you are remembered in heaven when you remember.
